scope: Actual HTTP/PostgreSQL authentication and concurrency; not browser coverage. Synthetic users only; no auth response bodies/tokens/credentials stored.

results.name: health, anonymous and invalid bearer responses preserve existing behavior
invalid credentials and malformed auth input preserve 401 and 400
username and email login retain JSON response fields and bearer identity
sequential refresh rotates once and logout invalidates exactly supplied tokens
old-session logout does not revoke a newly logged-in session
first-login burst and repeated username/email concurrent logins all succeed with one surviving refresh
the same refresh submitted concurrently is consumed exactly once
login racing an old refresh leaves the new login refresh valid
logout racing new login invalidates the old access while preserving the new session
logout racing refresh preserves existing exact-token revocation semantics
duplicate parallel logout with and without refresh is idempotent
crossed-user token logout payloads terminate without deadlock or broader revocation
expired and revoked refresh tokens return 401 on actual database state
results.mode: HTTP assertions with explicit SQL expiry/revocation fixture

results.name: account lockout retains failed-attempt policy under concurrent wrong passwords
